Nothing implemented; these are the facts and my suggestions. The run was two reading mistakes away from 100, both made by the single ERP worker.

## The run in numbers

| | 100-point run | Same package, run again | Latest run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quality | 100 | 70.1 | 78.8 |
| Model calls | 459 | 407 | 220 |
| Cost | $0.748 | $0.566 | $0.368 |
| Time | 15:38 | 14:30 | 7:39 |
| Cost × time | 702 | 493 | 169 |

- **The 100 was not stable.** The unchanged 100-point package was test-run once more and scored 70.1, with different mistakes (a withdrawn answer, the metal index, a bonus). One run says little about quality, for either version.
- **Rank:** 169 would be 4th place at quality 100. This was a test run, so the leaderboard still shows the 100.

## What went well

- **One worker per website:** 4 workers instead of 8. Records on the board fell from 172 to 88, with no repeats. Gathering took 332 seconds instead of 682.
- **Shorter records:** 22 records carry a note, against 91. The model wrote 34,000 tokens instead of 91,000.
- **No answer lost at the 60-second limit**, which had cost one worker six minutes before.
- **Bid form:** no more screenshot and clicking by coordinates; 126 seconds instead of 254. It still takes about three calls per form page.
- **Caveat:** the platform itself was faster this time (a typical call took 2.4 seconds, 4.4 before), so part of the time gain is not ours. The call count and cost are.

## What went wrong: 21.2 points, two mistakes

1. **Three base prices came out 1,000 times too small (19.9 points with everything that depends on them).**
   - The page shows `64,853 (en-US)` per 100 pieces. The worker recorded `64.853`, with a dot and without the tag, so the code read 64.853 and the price became 0.71 instead of 705.15.
   - The same happened to `186,615`.
   - The German-format prices were copied exactly.
2. **One lead time, 1 week instead of 11 (1.3 points).**
   - For three materials the worker recorded the stock total from the overview page (95, 99, 139), which includes blocked stock, instead of the available figure (29, 31, 51).
   - For four other materials the same worker recorded the available figure.

Every other field scored full points.

## Where we messed up

- **My answer-reading patch had a bad limit.** I let an answer pause for at most 25 seconds. This run shows the model's tool-call answers arrive in one piece at the end: two healthy answers of 28 and 30 seconds were thrown away at 25 seconds and asked again. It cost little today because the model was fast; on a slow day it would stall workers. My reviewers caught this after I had handed the patch over, and the correction had not reached you.
- **The "no explanations" wording went too far.** Your package says "Report values only: no explanations or quotes"; the sentence that named the format tag is gone. In the 100-point run the model kept the tag and worked out the format in its note. I can't prove cause from one run, but this is the likeliest reason for mistake 1, and my patch pushed in that direction.
- **One worker per site removed the second reading.** Before, three ERP workers recorded each price four or five times and the last record won. Now one misreading goes straight into the bid.
- **Changes I did not propose** are also in the package: history cut sooner (60,000 instead of 90,000 characters), shorter page text, a review-page check, Q&A answer numbers. One run cannot separate their effect.

## Suggestions, most useful first

1. **Check recorded numbers against the page, in code.** A number in a record must appear character for character on a page that worker read; otherwise the record is refused with what the page shows. This would have caught mistake 1 and costs no model calls unless it triggers.
2. **Restore the copying rule in the instructions:** copy every number exactly as shown, with its separators and format tag, and never convert it. Keep the ban on explanations.
3. **A second reading of only the deciding values:** after gathering, a fresh worker re-reads the price and stock of each chosen material, and a disagreement triggers a third reading. I estimate about ten calls and two cents. It brings back the second opinion and could catch mistake 2.
4. **Record both stock figures** (total and available), so the code can flag a material where only the total was read.
5. **Remove the 25-second pause limit:** make it equal to the whole-answer limit and keep 60 seconds for an answer to begin.
6. **Two corrections my reviewers confirmed:**
   - The collapsed-section fix can fill a hidden field when a visible one has the same label.
   - The lone mail worker should be told when its "not authorized" flag alone keeps a message out of the calculation.
7. **Judge versions on three runs each, not one.** The platform also has a "best of three" setting for the final, currently set to one attempt; it is worth checking how that is scored.

Suggestions 2 to 4 and the mail worker correction change what the model is told, so they need test runs. The handover folder is unchanged and still has the 25-second limit. Tell me which of these to prepare.

Three things I did not decide for you:

- **Item 3, refuse or only warn.** I wrote "refuse once, accept the second identical report". If you would rather never refuse a record, it can be a warning in the tool's reply instead; that is weaker but cannot cost a call.

Written for: the same Claude Code session as the list above.

The review of my four patches has finished. Everything it confirmed that matters is already in the list (items 1, 4 and 5), except two items. Neither would have changed the 78.8 score; take them or leave them.

```text
Two optional additions to the six changes above.

7. Handle an answer that was cut off at the output limit     [code only; tested here offline]
   Fact:   an answer that reaches the limit of 2,500 output tokens ends with
           finish reason "length". streamed() passes it on like a finished
           answer, so the worker stores half a tool call, fails to parse it and
           tells the model only "JSONDecodeError". The model is never told its
           answer was too long, and the broken call is re-sent with every later
           request. Not hit in run run_8614349eb83b71eb (longest answer 1,325
           tokens); the 100-point run had answers of up to 2,304.
   Change: rfq_agent.py: return the finish reason from streamed(). In worker(),
           when it is "length", do not store or run the answer; add a user
           message saying the answer was cut off and must be sent again in
           smaller parts (fewer records or steps per call), then continue.

8. Ask for one sentence in the "done" tool                   [prompt; needs a test run]
   Fact:   nothing in the code reads a worker's closing summary beyond printing
           its first 300 characters, and gathering ends only when the last
           worker's "done" arrives. In run run_8614349eb83b71eb that last
           summary was 981 tokens and took 12 s with nothing else running; in
           the 100-point run it was 2,164 tokens and 35 s.
   Change: rfq_agent.py, description of the "done" tool: the records are
           already on the board, so do not repeat them; one short sentence
           naming only what is unresolved.
```

Written for: the same Claude Code session as the two lists above.

The cost analysis of the 100-point run has finished. Your new run has overtaken most of it, since it already contains the changes it recommends. Two things from its skeptics are worth passing on: a correction to item 1 of my list and one new item. Everything else in my lists stands.

```text
Correction to item 1, and one more item.

1. (corrected) One answer limit instead of a pause limit, but not 240 seconds
   Why the correction: ask() tries three times. A tool-call answer sends nothing
           while it is being written, so a request that hangs after its first
           piece cannot be told from a long answer. With a 240 s limit such a
           hang would block a worker for 12 minutes.
   Change: rfq_agent.py: no separate pause limit. Whole-answer limit 150 s for
           the workers that gather evidence: a full answer of 2,500 tokens at
           the slowest speed measured (18 tokens a second) needs 139 s. 60 s
           for the submitter, whose longest answer so far took 10 s.
           FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT = 60 as before.
```

"""Download the platform's read-only records of many runs in one session.

python fetch_runs.py <folder> <list_runs.txt> [extra run ids ...]
For every run in the list that cost at least five cents (and every extra id) it saves, under <folder>/<run id>/:
get_run.txt, calls.txt, logs.txt, profile.txt and, for runs that did not finish with a score, diagnose.txt.
Only reading tools are called.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from pathlib import Path

ATIRA = os.path.join(os.environ["LOCALAPPDATA"], "atira", "bin", "atira.cmd")
folder = Path(sys.argv[1])
listing = Path(sys.argv[2]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
runs = []
for line in listing.splitlines():
    found = re.match(r"(run_\w+)\s+(\w+)\s+(\w+)\s+(.*?)\s+\$([\d.]+)\s+([\d:]+)", line)
    if found and float(found.group(5)) >= 0.05:
        runs.append((found.group(1), found.group(3)))
runs += [(run, "extra") for run in sys.argv[3:] if run not in {r for r, _ in runs}]

process = subprocess.Popen(["cmd", "/c", ATIRA, "mcp"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                           stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, encoding="utf-8", bufsize=1)
watchdog = threading.Timer(1500, process.kill)
watchdog.start()
counter = 0


def call(method, params=None, notify=False):
    global counter
    message = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
    if params is not None:
        message["params"] = params
    if not notify:
        counter += 1
        message["id"] = counter
    process.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
    process.stdin.flush()
    if notify:
        return None
    for line in process.stdout:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("{"):
            reply = json.loads(line)
            if reply.get("id") == counter:
                return reply
    raise SystemExit("the server closed")


def tool(name, **arguments):
    reply = call("tools/call", {"name": name, "arguments": arguments})
    result = reply.get("result", {})
    return "\n".join(part.get("text", "") for part in result.get("content", []) if part.get("type") == "text")


def all_logs(run):
    """The whole kept log: pages of 1000 lines, continued from the last time printed."""
    text = tool("run_logs", run_id=run, stream="stdout", limit=1000)
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for _ in range(6):
        footer = re.search(r"(\d+) of (\d+) matching lines", text)
        stamps = re.findall(r"^\[(\d+:\d+\.\d+)\]", text, re.M)
        if not footer or int(footer.group(1)) >= int(footer.group(2)) or not stamps:
            break
        text = tool("run_logs", run_id=run, stream="stdout", limit=1000, **{"from": stamps[-1]})
        fresh = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line not in set(lines[-400:])]
        if not fresh:
            break
        lines += fresh
    return "\n".join(lines)


try:
    call("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "log-reader", "version": "0"}})
    call("notifications/initialized", notify=True)
    for run, status in runs:
        target = folder / run
        target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if (target / "logs.txt").exists():
            continue
        (target / "get_run.txt").write_text(tool("get_run", run_id=run), encoding="utf-8")
        (target / "calls.txt").write_text(tool("run_llm_calls", run_id=run, limit=1000), encoding="utf-8")
        (target / "profile.txt").write_text(tool("run_profile", run_id=run, bucket="1m"), encoding="utf-8")
        if status != "finished" and status != "scored":
            (target / "diagnose.txt").write_text(tool("diagnose_run", run_id=run), encoding="utf-8")
        (target / "logs.txt").write_text(all_logs(run), encoding="utf-8")
        print(run, status, "saved", flush=True)
finally:
    watchdog.cancel()
    process.kill()

"""One compact report per run from the platform's records: python run_report.py <run folder> [--steps]

Reads get_run.txt, calls.txt and logs.txt (and diagnose.txt when present). Times are mm:ss on the run's clock.
"""
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

folder = Path(sys.argv[1])
show_steps = "--steps" in sys.argv
CALL = re.compile(r"\[(\d+):(\d+\.\d+) \+([\d.]+)s(?: wait ([\d.]+)s)?\] \S+ (\d+) in ([\d,]+)(?: \(cached ([\d,]+)\))? out ([\d,]+) \$([\d.]+)")
LOG = re.compile(r"\[(\d+):(\d+\.\d+)\] stdout: (.*)")
STEP = re.compile(r"\[([\w-]+)\] step (\d+): (\w+)(?: \[([\w-]+)\])?")
WORKER = re.compile(r"\[([\w-]+)\] ")


def clock(value):
    return f"{int(value // 60):02d}:{value % 60:04.1f}"


def read(name):
    path = folder / name
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if path.exists() else ""


summary = read("get_run.txt")
calls = []
for line in read("calls.txt").splitlines():
    found = CALL.match(line.strip())
    if found:
        start = int(found.group(1)) * 60 + float(found.group(2))
        calls.append({"start": start, "took": float(found.group(3)), "end": start + float(found.group(3)), "status": found.group(5),
                      "new": int(found.group(6).replace(",", "")), "cached": int((found.group(7) or "0").replace(",", "")),
                      "out": int(found.group(8).replace(",", "")), "cost": float(found.group(9))})
log = []
for line in read("logs.txt").splitlines():
    found = LOG.match(line)
    if found:
        log.append((int(found.group(1)) * 60 + float(found.group(2)), found.group(3)))

print("=" * 118)
head = summary.splitlines()
print(head[0] if head else folder.name)
for line in head[1:8]:
    if line.startswith(("Status", "Started", "LLM", "Score", "Failure", "Error")) or "failure" in line.lower():
        print("  " + line[:230])
lost = [line.strip() for line in head if re.search(r": 0 \(|: 0$", line) and "extra_positions" not in line]
entered = [line for line in head if re.match(r"\s+positions\[[\d.]+\]: ", line)]

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   **Standing context (Atira EHL hackathon, challenge "rfq", "From RFQ to bid"):** repo `C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\GitHub\The-Last-Team`, my branch `claude-build` (package `.\my-agent`). The team's real candidate is a teammate's agent (a different code line), which I analyse and prepare patches for; my own branch is a lab.

   **Hard rules stated by the user (verbatim, still in force):**
   - "Keep everything local: never push, never touch remotes."
   - "Never run a scored submission without my explicit approval. Test runs are fine (up to 4 at once)." — later overridden for now by: "the platform is going some performance upgrades right now, so we do not run anything. I'll tell you when to run." (I have started no test run since; the user's later sentence "to questions.run any test run right now" was ambiguous, I asked, it was never clarified. Do NOT start runs.)
   - "Never put values seen on the public websites (references, material numbers, prices, logins, TANs, hostnames) anywhere in the repo, including tests and prompts."
   - "Stop at every ⚑ checkpoint in the brief and ask me. If anything is ambiguous, ask me directly."
   - "Commit locally on claude-build after each working step; update PROGRESS.md after each milestone."
   - "do not create too many tests and safeguards, we need a simple lightweight, yet smart system. do not check literally everything."
   - "we are not submitting anything from our branch yet, we are just testing and we are seeing locally."
   - "If you have any other questions, ask me directly. do not assume things on your own."
   - Design principle from the user: one worker per website, one reading is enough ("we don't need to cross-reference in general from different workers in the same page because we assume the Qwen model is good enough to ... read the right thing at once"); no second readings, no multi-run comparisons.
   - Priorities: "The rank among the hundreds matter ... the most" (ranking = eligible, then quality, then LLM cost × run time), and the agent "does not overfit. And does not have any hard-coded things to score better on the dataset we have" (final ranking is on a private dataset).
   - Ultracode was ON for most of the session; the latest system reminder says "Ultracode is off — the Workflow tool's standard opt-in rule applies again" (so no Workflow unless the user opts in).

   **Most recent request (current task, verbatim):** "alright, ,we have had a bunch of runs with different setups and things / what do you think about them? / go through all of the main runs that scored above 35 ig and figure out what went right and what went wrong. pick out the biggest bottlenecks, and what's going wrong the most. don't suggest fixes or implement anything yet, just give an analysis of what step each call and how much time and energy it wasted on, how long it stopped for, how long was the agent stuck on one page and which page and when everything. / there were runs where the scouting and everything was quite quick but then it was stuck on the submission and then couldn't submit anything at all. look at those as well, if you have any questions, ask me directly."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Atira platform: CLI at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin\atira.cmd` (wrap in `Start-Job` with timeout); `atira mcp` serves read-only debugging tools over stdio: `list_runs(kind, limit≤50)`, `get_run`, `diagnose_run`, `run_logs(run_id, from, to, stream, grep, limit≤1000)`, `run_llm_calls(limit≤1000)`, `run_profile(bucket=30s|1m|5m)`, `run_inputs`, `run_screenshot`, `compare_runs(a,b)`, `list_submissions`, `get_submission`, `run_package`, `leaderboard(compare_run)`; never call `test_run`, `cancel_run`, `submit`, `final`.
   - Ranking: eligible first, then quality, then LLM cost × run time ($·s). "the latest submission that passes review goes into the final run on the private dataset." `final [--best-of 1|3]` exists (currently best_of 1).
   - Scoring: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, consistency 5, withdrawn-answer 5, index-window 5, each position 13 (material 2.6, quantity 1.95, base price 1.95, surcharge/packaging/rebate/unit price/lead time 1.3 each).
   - Qwen prices per million tokens: new input $0.15, cached input $0.016, output $0.47. A call costs about 2.4 s fixed plus 19–32 s per 1,000 output tokens; the platform's "queue wait" figure is NOT a queue time (equals latency minus ~0.4 s). Tool-call answers arrive in one piece at the end of the stream (measured in run_8614349eb83b71eb).
   - Platform keeps only the tail of a run's stdout (~110–190 KB); `run_llm_calls` and `run_inputs` cover the whole run.
   - Teammate's agent (18-file packages): `rfq_agent.py` (plan → investigators per website → `pricing.calculate_bid` → submit worker), `browser_tools.py` (`inspect`, `fill_many`, `form_sequence`, `_locate`, `dismiss_blocking_dialogs`, `read_pages`, `paginate`), `pricing.py` (`RECORD_GUIDE`, `number`, `when`, `day_end`, `Evidence`, `calculate_bid`), `models.py`, `agent.json`. result.output:
- challenge_brief(challenge): The challenge as Markdown: the task, the websites, the rules and limits, the run contract (environment, browsers and time limits), how answers are submitted and scored, and the answer schema. Ranking: eligible answers first, then quality, then LLM cost � run time. About 6k tokens.
- list_runs(kind, limit): Your team's recent test runs and scored runs, newest first: id, kind, status, quality and eligibility, LLM cost, run time, start and the package (its SHA-256 and label). Use get_run for one run, diagnose_run for why it failed.
- get_run(run_id): One run in full: status, phase and failure, its place in the queue or the free models' warm-up while it waits, phase starts on the run's clock, the package, LLM calls by model with failures and queue waits, the score with points per field (test runs), the recordings, the answer it entered, and the run page URL (?t=mm:ss opens the replay there). About 1�2k tokens.
- diagnose_run(run_id): Why a run failed and what to do next, in one call: the failure class and whether a rerun as it is would help, the last 20 lines of stdout and stderr, the answer, model errors by status, stretches over 60 s with no input, no screen change and no model call, and browsers whose screen froze. About 2�3k tokens.
- run_logs(run_id, from, to, stream, grep, browser, tail, limit, after): A run's log lines, in time order, each with its time on the run's clock and its stream. Streams: stdout and stderr (your agent system), setup (the platform: install, the free models' warm-up), input (what the browsers received; run_inputs reads them better, so they're left out unless you ask). Narrow with from/to (e.g. from 02:10 to 02:40), grep, browser; tail for the last lines; page with after. 
- run_llm_calls(run_id, from, to, model, status, limit, after): Every model call of a run, one line each: time on the run's clock, latency, queue wait (hosted models), model, status, tokens (cached), cost and id. The header has the time in calls, p50/p95 latency, the most calls at once, failures by status and the hosted models' queue waits. Filter by from/to, model and status (ok, error, all); page with after. About 35 tokens a call.
- run_profile(run_id, bucket, browser): Where a run's time went, bucket by bucket (30 s, 1 min or 5 min): per browser, its inputs and how long its screen was changing (� idle); model calls, seconds in calls and cost. Then the critical path: the longest stretches with nothing happening, the slowest calls, and when each browser went quiet. About 1.5�3k tokens.
- run_screenshot(run_id, at, browser, frames, marks): A browser's screen at a time in the run, cut from its recording, with the clicks just before it marked (red: the latest) and the log lines around it. browser "all" puts every browser in one 2�2 image; frames {from, to, every} makes a filmstrip of up to 9 frames in one image. While a run is still going there is no recording yet: it shows the latest live frame. About 1.5k tokens an image.
- run_inputs(run_id, browser, from, to, limit, after): What the agent system did in the browsers, as the platform recorded it: clicks and taps with x,y on the 1280�800 display (Chrome's bar included), drags, scrolls and typing, each with its time on the run's clock, in time order. Typed text shows, with keys and tokens masked. Pair a time with run_screenshot to see the screen then.
- compare_runs(a, b): Two runs side by side (A, then B, and how B differs): package, status, quality, time, cost, cost � time, calls and failures, phase times, calls and cost per model, the score's points per field that changed, and the answer's fields that changed. About 1�2k tokens.
- wait_for_run(run_id, until, timeout_s): Wait until a run is running (its agent system has started) or done, then say how it stands; while it waits it sends progress. Gives up after timeout_s (default 50 s, at most 600: raise it if your client allows long tool calls) and says where the run is, so you can call it again.
- list_submissions(challenge, limit): Your team's scored submissions, newest first: id, when, review status, any organizer note, status, quality and eligibility with cost and time, and the package. The reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers. get_submission shows one with its runs.
- get_submission(submission_id): One scored submission: its review status and any organizer note (the reviewer's reasons stay with the organizers), its runs with their status, place in the queue and score, and the package. Takes a sub_ id.
- run_package(run_id, out): The package a test run, scored run or submission of your team used, exactly as uploaded: its SHA-256 and label, agent.json, and every file's path and size (never the contents). With out, it also saves the .tar.gz in that folder, checked against its SHA-256; unpack it with tar to read the files. About 15 tokens a file.
- leaderboard(challenge, limit, compare_run): The leaderboard (on the public dataset during the hackathon) with each entry's cost � time and the Pareto front, your team's rank and the gap to the next rank. compare_run: where one of your runs would rank if it were your team's entry. Ranking: eligible first, then quality, then LLM cost � run time.
- models(): The models the organizers host for free, whether each is up, and how to call them from your computer through `atira models proxy` (the variables to export). Calls from your computer are free, recorded and never ranked.
- test_run(dir, label, challenge): Pack a folder and start a test run: it runs once in the same sandbox as scored runs, on the public scenario, and never counts for the leaderboard. Returns the run id, its place in the queue, the package's SHA-256 and label (the git commit by default) and its page; then wait_for_run, run_logs and run_screenshot.
- cancel_run(run_id, confirm): Cancel one of your team's test or scored runs that has not finished: its sandbox is removed and the run fails as cancelled; its logs stay. A cancelled scored run doesn't come back, so this needs confirm: true; ask the person first for a scored run.
- submit(dir, confirm, label, challenge): Pack a folder and submit it for a scored run. This is public and can't be undone: it is reviewed, run once on the public dataset and ranked on the public leaderboard under the team's name, and the latest submission that passes review goes into the final run on the private dataset. Before calling, tell the person exactly that and get an explicit yes for this package, then call with confirm: true. U

python mcp_call.py list
python mcp_call.py <tool> '<json arguments>' [out file]

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading

ATIRA = os.path.join(os.environ["LOCALAPPDATA"], "atira", "bin", "atira.cmd")
# Tools that start, cancel or submit something are never called from here.
FORBIDDEN = ("submit", "test_run", "cancel", "final")


def main():
    tool = sys.argv[1]
    if tool != "list" and any(word in tool for word in FORBIDDEN):
        raise SystemExit(f"refusing to call {tool}")
    process = subprocess.Popen(["cmd", "/c", ATIRA, "mcp"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                               stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, encoding="utf-8", bufsize=1)
    timer = threading.Timer(float(os.environ.get("MCP_TIMEOUT", "120")), process.kill)
    timer.start()

    def send(message):
        process.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
        process.stdin.flush()

    def answer(wanted):
        for line in process.stdout:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line.startswith("{"):
                continue
            message = json.loads(line)
            if message.get("id") == wanted:
                return message
        raise SystemExit("the server closed without answering")

    try:
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize", "params": {
            "protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "log-reader", "version": "0"}}})
        answer(1)
        send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})
        if tool == "list":
            send({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/list"})
            for item in answer(2)["result"]["tools"]:
                properties = item.get("inputSchema", {}).get("properties", {})
                print(f"- {item['name']}({', '.join(properties)}): {item.get('description', '')[:400]}")
            return
        # Arguments as key=value words (a shell mangles quoted JSON); "out=<file>" saves the answer.
        arguments, out = {}, None
        for word in sys.argv[2:]:
            key, _, value = word.partition("=")
            if key == "out":
                out = value
                continue
            try:
                arguments[key] = json.loads(value)
            except ValueError:

"""Download what the browsers received in every saved run: python fetch_inputs.py <folder of run folders>

Saves <folder>/<run id>/inputs.txt. Only the reading tool run_inputs is called.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from pathlib import Path

ATIRA = os.path.join(os.environ["LOCALAPPDATA"], "atira", "bin", "atira.cmd")
folder = Path(sys.argv[1])
runs = sorted(item.name for item in folder.iterdir() if item.is_dir() and item.name.startswith("run_"))

process = subprocess.Popen(["cmd", "/c", ATIRA, "mcp"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                           stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, encoding="utf-8", bufsize=1)
watchdog = threading.Timer(900, process.kill)
watchdog.start()
counter = 0


def call(method, params=None, notify=False):
    global counter
    message = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
    if params is not None:
        message["params"] = params
    if not notify:
        counter += 1
        message["id"] = counter
    process.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
    process.stdin.flush()
    if notify:
        return None
    for line in process.stdout:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("{"):
            reply = json.loads(line)
            if reply.get("id") == counter:
                return reply
    raise SystemExit("the server closed")


def tool(name, **arguments):
    reply = call("tools/call", {"name": name, "arguments": arguments})
    result = reply.get("result", {})
    return "\n".join(part.get("text", "") for part in result.get("content", []) if part.get("type") == "text")


try:
    call("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "log-reader", "version": "0"}})
    call("notifications/initialized", notify=True)
    for run in runs:
        target = folder / run / "inputs.txt"
        if target.exists():
            continue
        text = tool("run_inputs", run_id=run, limit=1000)
        lines = text.splitlines()
        for _ in range(5):
            footer = re.search(r"(\d+) of (\d+) inputs", text)
            stamps = re.findall(r"^\[(\d+:\d+\.\d+)\]", text, re.M)
            if not footer or int(footer.group(1)) >= int(footer.group(2)) or not stamps:
                break
            text = tool("run_inputs", run_id=run, limit=1000, **{"from": stamps[-1]})
            seen = set(lines[-300:])
            fresh = [line for line in text.splitlines() if line not in seen]
            if not fresh:
                break
            lines += fresh
        target.write_text("\n".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
        print(run, len(lines), flush=True)
finally:
    watchdog.cancel()
    process.kill()

Shows every logged line of the workers whose name contains the word (default "submit") plus run-level marks,
from the given time on. Consecutive lines that differ only in numbers are folded into one with a count.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
import build_data as data  # noqa: E402

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
root, run_id = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
start = data.secs(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0
word = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "submit"
run = data.build(root / run_id)
rows = [e for e in run["events"] if e[0] >= start and (word in e[1] or e[2] == "mark" or (word == "submit" and e[1] in ("", "master")))]
print(f"{run_id} line {run['line']} · bid decided {data.clock(run['phase']['bidReady'])} · ended {data.clock(run['seconds'])} · {len(rows)} lines")
folded = []
for at, worker, kind, action, page, ok, text in rows:
    key = (worker, kind, action, re.sub(r"\d+", "N", text)[:60], ok)
    if folded and folded[-1]["key"] == key:
        folded[-1]["n"] += 1
        folded[-1]["to"] = at
    else:
        folded.append({"key": key, "n": 1, "at": at, "to": at, "worker": worker, "kind": kind, "action": action, "ok": ok, "text": text, "page": page})
previous = None
for item in folded:
    gap = f"+{item['at'] - previous:4.0f}s" if previous is not None else "      "
    times = data.clock(item["at"]) + (f"-{data.clock(item['to'])} x{item['n']}" if item["n"] > 1 else "")

"""The submitter's timeline of one run, repeats folded: python subline.py <runs folder> <run id> [from mm:ss] [worker word]

Shows the logged actions of the workers whose name contains the word (default "submit") plus run-level marks,
from the given time on. Model answers are counted, not listed. Consecutive actions of one kind are folded
into one line with a count and up to three of their texts.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
import build_data as data  # noqa: E402

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
root, run_id = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
start = data.secs(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 0
word = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "submit"
run = data.build(root / run_id)
rows = [e for e in run["events"] if e[0] >= start and (word in e[1] or e[2] == "mark")]
print(f"{run_id} line {run['line']} · bid decided {data.clock(run['phase']['bidReady'])} · ended {data.clock(run['seconds'])}")
folded, answers = [], 0
for at, worker, kind, action, page, ok, text in rows:
    if kind == "model":
        answers += 1
        if folded:
            folded[-1]["answers"] += 1
        continue
    if kind == "mark" and re.match(r"(phase left|candidate left|calc_round)", text):
        continue
    key = (worker, kind, action, ok)
    if folded and folded[-1]["key"] == key and kind != "mark":
        folded[-1]["n"] += 1
        folded[-1]["to"] = at
        if text not in folded[-1]["texts"]:
            folded[-1]["texts"].append(text)
    else:
        folded.append({"key": key, "n": 1, "at": at, "to": at, "worker": worker, "kind": kind, "action": action, "ok": ok, "texts": [text], "page": page, "answers": 0})
previous = None
for item in folded:
    gap = f"+{item['at'] - previous:4.0f}s" if previous is not None else "      "
    times = data.clock(item["at"]) + (f"-{data.clock(item['to'])} x{item['n']}" if item["n"] > 1 else "")
    flag = "" if item["ok"] else "FAILED "
    texts = " | ".join(text[:int(170 / min(3, len(item["texts"])))] for text in item["texts"][:3]) + (f" | +{len(item['texts']) - 3} more" if len(item["texts"]) > 3 else "")
    print(f"{times:17s} {gap} {item['worker'][:10]:10s} {flag}{item['kind']} {item['action'][:20]}: {texts}" + (f" @ {item['page'][:44]}" if item["page"] else ""))
    previous = item["to"]
print(f"model answers in this stretch: {answers}")

"""Save screenshots from runs' recordings: python shot.py <out folder> <run id>@<mm:ss>[@browser] ...

Calls only the reading tool run_screenshot. browser is 1-4 or "all" (default all: the four screens in one image).
"""
import base64
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
from pathlib import Path

ATIRA = os.path.join(os.environ["LOCALAPPDATA"], "atira", "bin", "atira.cmd")
out = Path(sys.argv[1])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
process = subprocess.Popen(["cmd", "/c", ATIRA, "mcp"], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                           stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True, encoding="utf-8", bufsize=1)
watchdog = threading.Timer(600, process.kill)
watchdog.start()
counter = 0


def call(method, params=None, notify=False):
    global counter
    message = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method}
    if params is not None:
        message["params"] = params
    if not notify:
        counter += 1
        message["id"] = counter
    process.stdin.write(json.dumps(message) + "\n")
    process.stdin.flush()
    if notify:
        return None
    for line in process.stdout:
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("{"):
            reply = json.loads(line)
            if reply.get("id") == counter:
                return reply
    raise SystemExit("the server closed")


try:
    call("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "log-reader", "version": "0"}})
    call("notifications/initialized", notify=True)
    for word in sys.argv[2:]:
        parts = word.split("@")
        run, at, browser = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else "all"
        arguments = {"run_id": run, "at": at, "browser": int(browser) if browser.isdigit() else browser}
        result = call("tools/call", {"name": "run_screenshot", "arguments": arguments}).get("result", {})
        name = f"{run[4:10]}_{at.replace(':', '')}_{browser}"
        for part in result.get("content", []):
            if part.get("type") == "image":
                (out / f"{name}.png").write_bytes(base64.b64decode(part["data"]))
            elif part.get("type") == "text":
                (out / f"{name}.txt").write_text(part["text"], encoding="utf-8")
        print(name, [part.get("type") for part in result.get("content", [])], flush=True)
finally:
    watchdog.cancel()
    process.kill()

"""Cross-run figures from the saved records: python aggregate.py <runs folder>"""
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
import build_data as data  # noqa: E402

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
root = Path(sys.argv[1])
runs = [data.build(folder) for folder in sorted(root.iterdir()) if folder.is_dir() and (folder / "get_run.txt").exists()]
runs.sort(key=lambda run: -(run["quality"] or -1))
clock = data.clock

print("== runs with an answer, best first: quality | cost | time | gathering s/$ | deciding s/$ | submitting s/$/calls | calls | new tokens per qwen call | $·s")
for run in runs:
    if not run["answer"]:
        continue
    split = run.get("split", {})

    qwen = next((m for m in run["llm"]["models"] if "qwen" in m["name"]), None)

"""Open the local report in a headless browser, report script errors and save screenshots.

python check_page.py <index.html> <out folder> [route[@width[@theme]] ...]
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

page_file = Path(sys.argv[1]).resolve()
out = Path(sys.argv[2])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
routes = sys.argv[3:] or ["overview", "runs", "stuck", "run"]
problems = []
with sync_playwright() as play:
    browser = play.chromium.launch()
    for word in routes:
        parts = word.split("@")
        route, width, theme = parts[0], int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 1280, parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 else "light"
        context = browser.new_context(viewport={"width": width, "height": 900}, color_scheme=theme)
        page = context.new_page()
        page.on("console", lambda message: problems.append(f"{word}: console {message.type}: {message.text}") if message.type in ("error", "warning") else None)
        page.on("pageerror", lambda error: problems.append(f"{word}: page error: {error}"))
        page.goto(page_file.as_uri() + "#" + route)
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)
        overflow = page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth - window.innerWidth")
        name = route.replace("/", "_") + f"_{width}_{theme}.png"
        page.screenshot(path=str(out / name), full_page=True)
        print(f"{word}: saved {name}, page height {page.evaluate('document.documentElement.scrollHeight')}, sideways overflow {overflow}px")
        context.close()
    browser.close()

---
name: run-report-dashboard
description: Where the cross-run analysis dashboard for the rfq challenge lives and how to rebuild it after new runs
metadata:
  type: reference
---

The cross-run analysis dashboard (HTML, CSS, JS, no build step) is in
`C:\Users\Administrator\Documents\GitHub\The-Last-Team-run-report\`, a sibling of the repository, outside it on purpose:
its log lines hold values seen on the practice sites, which must never enter the repo. Open `index.html` directly.

Contents: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `app.js`, `data.js` (generated), `notes.json` (the written analysis per run and
across runs, hand-maintained), `records/<run id>/` (platform records: get_run, calls, logs, inputs, profile, diagnose),
`tools/` (the generators), `img/` (screenshots cut from recordings).

Rebuild after new runs, from that folder, with the package interpreter (`my-agent\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`):

1. `tools/mcp_call.py list_runs kind=all limit=50 out=records/list_runs.txt`

content.text:
**Verdict:** the system is not stable yet. 25 of the 44 runs never entered an answer, and they took $6.01 of the $13.56 spent and 349 of 563 minutes. No package that ran twice scored the same twice (100 and 70.1; 98.7 and 35.6).

The dashboard is at [../The-Last-Team-run-report/index.html](../The-Last-Team-run-report/index.html) — open the file directly. It has four tabs: Overview, Runs, Stuck, and a Run detail page with timeline, per-worker steps, failures, points per field and the log. It opens without script errors at desktop and phone width.

The runs come from four different code lines, which I labelled by package contents (run ids below are the first six characters after `run_`):

| Line | What it is | Runs | Answers | Best | Median cost | Median time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | the scored `rfq_agent` line, Qwen only | 18 | 13 | 100 | $0.538 | 13:41 |
| B | compact rewrite, Qwen + Clef | 6 | 4 | 98.7 | $0.110 | 06:14 |
| C | master/worker/factboard, first version | 4 | 0 | – | $0.460 | 19:55 |
| D | same family, grown | 9 | 2 | 15 | $0.190 | 16:18 |

Seven early runs from two other packages never got an answer in.

## Biggest bottlenecks

1. **Submission is where runs die.** Every run that gathered and then entered nothing falls under one of four causes (table below).
2. **Gathering is mostly the mailbox.** In line A, gathering is 63–84% of run time in nine of ten runs and 70–94% of the money. In `2bb96f` one mail worker took 162 steps and $0.309 of $0.588 for one record.
3. **The money is fresh input tokens.** They are 52–83% of every line A bill; output is 3–6%. Clef is not free in a run: it is 39% of the best line B run's cost.
4. **When gathering stops decides the score.** Runs cut near 200 s finish fast but leave positions out (`e42aa3`: 2 of 5 entered). In line B, `f54765` spent 30 s on a follow-up round and scored 98.7; `0c030b`, the same package, decided with 25 gaps open and scored 35.6.
5. **Points go to wrong readings more than missing ones.** Among the 19 answers, the metal index window was lost in 14 and lead time in 12. Lead time is the only loss in both 98.7 runs. Four runs stated "no gaps" and still lost 30–45 points.

## Stuck in submission

| Cause | Run | Stuck for | What happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| Own guard refuses the final click (C) | `ecdefb` | 10 min 6 s | 48 clicks answered "Verify the answer and review before final commit" |
| Nothing to enter (D) | `6fbc4e` | 9 min 41 s | 73 clicks on form step 1, no typing, page says "Bieter nicht registriert" |
| Position step of the form (A) | `d6bc7e` | 5 min 36 s | stroke sent 23 times while its drop-down was still disabled |
| Position step of the form (A) | `71218c` | 7 min 8 s | 91 form steps with no error and no end |
| Signing code (B) | `4d92ec` | 11 min 32 s | code requested 8 times; the mail slider timed out 14 times |
| Signing code (D) | `6a96a6` | 6 min 7 s | waited for a code its helper never found |
| Signing code (A) | `1ee507` | – | two mail page timeouts; deadline hit 8 s after its last form step |

## What went right

- **`f54765` (line B):** 98.7 for $0.135 in 06:14, which is 50 $·s against the scored 100's 702. The form was opened while research ran and filled by code in 99 s with no model call.
- **Line A's signing:** it reads the code in 5–9 s in its three best runs.
- **Line A's number check:** it refused 9 records in the 98.7 run `3a3d06`.

Eleven teams hold 100 points, so anything under 100 ranks below all of them whatever it costs.

## Limits and housekeeping

- The platform keeps only the tail of each agent log, so step detail starts where the log starts. Calls and browser inputs cover the whole run.
- I started no runs, and the repository is untouched. The report folder sits outside it because its log lines contain values from the practice sites; for the same reason I did not publish it anywhere.
- The folder also holds the run records and generator scripts, so it can be rebuilt after new runs.

## Questions

1. Who owns which code line? I can then label them by name instead of A–D.
2. Six runs were cancelled by teammates. I counted them as "the agent was stuck at that moment" — is that right for all six?

alright, which do you think is the best run? the 100 or 98.7?
which one is better and why?

**The 100 is the better result; the 98.7 run `f54765` is the better run.** Which one counts depends on whether you are asking about the leaderboard today or about what to build on.

| | `19df26` (the 100) | `f54765` (98.7) | `3a3d06` (98.7) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Code line | A, scored line | B, compact Qwen + Clef | A, scored line |
| Cost | $0.748 | $0.135 | $0.497 |
| Time | 15:38 | 06:14 | 08:33 |
| Cost × time | 702 $·s | 50 $·s | 255 $·s |
| Model calls | 459 | 212 | 347 |
| Points lost | none | one lead time (1.3) | one lead time (1.3) |
| Same package, other run | 70.1 | 35.6 | not run twice |
| Rank on today's board | 11 | 12 | 12 |

**Why the 100 is the better result:** ranking puts quality before cost × time. Eleven teams hold 100, so any 98.7 sits below all of them at rank 12, however cheap it is. One wrong lead time costs more rank than a 14-fold saving in cost × time earns.

**Why `f54765` is the better run:**
- It did the same job for 18% of the money and 40% of the time.
- It missed 100 by a single field.
- The 100 is last among the 100s, and the ten ahead of it sit between 1.2 and 437 $·s. Even if that package scored 100 every time, it would stay at the bottom of that group.
- A 100 at `f54765`'s cost and time would be rank 5.

**What speaks against `f54765`:** its package is the least proven. Its other run scored 35.6, a 63-point spread, against a 30-point spread for the 100's package. Line A also has the deeper record: ten runs at 35 or more against two for line B.

The other 98.7, `3a3d06`, matches `f54765`'s score at 3.7 times the cost, so it loses to `f54765` on every measure. It is still the best evidence that line A can be much cheaper than the 100 was: 255 against 702 $·s.

Both 98.7 runs lost the same kind of field, a lead time entered as 1 week.

So if I had to pick one to stand behind today, it is the 100, because it is the only one that has shown a full score. If I had to pick one to build on, it is `f54765`. Two runs per package is too few to trust either number.
alright, so out idea if to choose one of them, and fine tune it and make that one better, which one is a better one to copy and work on in our local system?

174	                    (self.purposes if qid[0] == "b" else self.fields)[(control.kind, control.label)] = answer["choice"]
175	            if "page" in answers:
176	                self.layouts[layout] = answers["page"]["choice"]
177	            if "position" in answers:
178	                found = [answers["position"]["choice"]]
179	        return self.layouts.get(layout, "form"), (found[0] if len(found) == 1 else None)

181	    def controls_for(self, obs: Observation, field: str) -> list:
182	        return [c for c in obs.controls.values() if self.fields.get((c.kind, c.label)) == field]
183	
184	    def button(self, obs: Observation, purpose: str):
185	        for control in obs.controls.values():
186	            if self.purposes.get((control.kind, control.label)) == purpose and not control.disabled:
187	                return control
188	        return None

190	    async def pick_option(self, control, field: str, value) -> str | None:
191	        options = [o for o in control.options or [] if o]
192	        key = (field, str(value), tuple(options))
193	        if key in self.options:
194	            return self.options[key]
195	        if field == "offer_type":
196	            want = "a regular main offer (decision bid)" if value == "bid" else "a declaration of non-participation (no bid)"
197	        else:
198	            chosen = match_option(value, options)
199	            if chosen or field in ("bore", "stroke", "pressure", "material", "lead_time"):
200	                self.options[key] = chosen
201	                return chosen
202	            want = f"{FIELDS[field]} = {value}"
203	        if len(options) < 2:
204	            return None
205	        answers = await llm.clef({"instructions": self.brief_submission, "field": FIELDS[field], "wanted": want},
206	                                 {"o": llm.choice(f"Which option means: {want}?", {str(i): o for i, o in enumerate(options)})})
207	        self.options[key] = options[int(answers["o"]["choice"])]
208	        return self.options[key]

210	    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- fill
211	    async def fill_selects(self, obs: Observation, values: dict) -> bool:
212	        """Set the first select (page order) whose value differs; True if one changed."""
213	        for control in sorted(obs.controls.values(), key=lambda c: c.id):
214	            field = self.fields.get((control.kind, control.label))
215	            if control.kind == "select" and field in values and not control.disabled:
216	                option = await self.pick_option(control, field, values[field])
217	                if option and normalize(option) != normalize(control.value or ""):
218	                    self.log(f"[submit] {field}: {await self.tab.select(control.id, option)}")
219	                    return True
220	        return False
221	
222	    async def fill_inputs(self, obs: Observation, values: dict) -> int:
223	        """Enter every text field and checkbox of this page in one pass (no round trip in between)."""
224	        changed = 0
225	        for control in sorted(obs.controls.values(), key=lambda c: c.id):
226	            field = self.fields.get((control.kind, control.label))
227	            if field not in values or control.disabled or control.kind == "select":
228	                continue
229	            if control.kind in ("checkbox", "radio", "switch"):
230	                if bool(control.checked) != bool(values[field]):
231	                    self.log(f"[submit] {field}: {await self.tab.check(control.id, bool(values[field]))}")
232	                    changed += 1
233	            elif normalize(control.value or "") != normalize(values[field]):
234	                self.log(f"[submit] {field}: {await self.tab.fill(control.id, values[field])}")
235	                changed += 1
236	        return changed

238	    def cascade_pending(self, obs: Observation, values: dict) -> bool:
239	        """A configuration select whose value is known is still disabled or lacks the option: apply first."""
240	        for control in obs.controls.values():
241	            field = self.fields.get((control.kind, control.label))
242	            if control.kind == "select" and field in CONFIGURATION and field in values:
243	                if control.disabled or (field in ("bore", "stroke", "pressure", "material")
244	                                        and not match_option(values[field], control.options or [])):
245	                    return True
246	        return False

248	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ run
249	    async def run(self, until: float, start_url: str = "") -> str | None:
250	        try:
251	            return await self._run(until, start_url)
252	        except Exception as error:  # the caller must always learn the outcome
253	            self.log(f"[submit] failed: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:300]}")
254	            return None
255	
256	    async def _run(self, until: float, start_url: str) -> str | None:
257	        if self.tab.page is None:
258	            self.log(f"[submit] {await self.tab.open(start_url)}")
259	        last, repeats, failures = None, 0, 0
260	        for _ in range(120):
261	            if llm.clock() > until:
262	                self.log("[submit] out of time")
263	                return None
264	            try:
265	                obs = await asyncio.wait_for(self.tab.observe(), 20)
266	                if obs.password:
267	                    self.log(f"[submit] {await self.tab.login()}")
268	                    continue
269	                kind, position = await self.understand(obs)
270	            except Exception as error:  # a flaky page: observe again, but not forever
271	                failures += 1
272	                self.log(f"[submit] page not readable ({type(error).__name__}); {'giving up' if failures > 5 else 'again'}")
273	                if failures > 5:
274	                    return None
275	                await asyncio.sleep(1)
276	                continue
277	            if kind == "form" and self.waits_for_bid(obs):
278	                self.log("[submit] form ready; waiting for the decided bid")
279	                try:
280	                    await asyncio.wait_for(self.ready.wait(), max(1.0, until - llm.clock()))
281	                except asyncio.TimeoutError:
282	                    self.log("[submit] no bid in time")
283	                    return None
284	                self.log("[submit] bid received; continuing")
285	                last, repeats = None, 0
286	                continue  # the page may have changed (session timeout) while waiting
287	            if kind == "receipt":
288	                self.log("[submit] receipt: " + " ".join(obs.text.split())[:300])
289	                return obs.text[:600]
290	            repeats = repeats + 1 if obs.signature == last else 0
291	            last = obs.signature
292	            if repeats >= 2:
293	                await self.repair(obs, position)
294	                continue
295	            if kind in ("obstacle", "start"):
296	                close = self.button(obs, "close")
297	                target = close.id if close and kind == "obstacle" else await self.choose(
298	                    obs, "start the offer submission for this tender (register participation first if required)"
299	                    if kind == "start" else "remove the obstacle")
300	                self.log(f"[submit] {kind}: {await self.tab.click(target)}")
301	                continue
302	            values = self.values_for(position)
303	            if position and position not in self.positions and self.button(obs, "omit"):
304	                self.log(f"[submit] omit {position}: {await self.tab.click(self.button(obs, 'omit').id)}")
305	                continue
306	            if await self.fill_selects(obs, values):
307	                continue
308	            if self.cascade_pending(obs, values) and self.button(obs, "apply"):
309	                self.log(f"[submit] apply: {await self.tab.click(self.button(obs, 'apply').id)}")
310	                continue
311	            await self.fill_inputs(obs, values)
312	            tan = self.controls_for(obs, "tan")
313	            if tan and not (tan[0].value or ""):
314	                if not self.tan_requested and self.button(obs, "request_tan") and self.tan_requests < 3:
315	                    self.log(f"[submit] {await self.tab.click(self.button(obs, 'request_tan').id)}")
316	                    self.tan_requested = True
317	                    self.tan_requests += 1
318	                    continue
319	                code = await self.fetch_tan(obs, until)
320	                if code:
321	                    self.log(f"[submit] {await self.tab.fill(tan[0].id, code)}")
322	                else:
323	                    self.tan_requested = False  # request a fresh one
324	                continue
325	            control = self.button(obs, "submit") if tan else None
326	            control = control or self.button(obs, "proceed")
327	            if control:
328	                self.log(f"[submit] {self.purposes[(control.kind, control.label)]}: {await self.tab.click(control.id)}")
329	            else:
330	                await self.repair(obs, position)
331	        return None
332	
333	    async def choose(self, obs: Observation, goal: str) -> int:
334	        options = {str(c.id): c.describe()[:160] for c in obs.controls.values() if not c.disabled}
335	        answers = await llm.clef({"goal": goal, "instructions": self.brief_submission, "page": obs.clip(6000)},
336	                                 {"c": llm.choice(f"Which control should be clicked to {goal}? Avoid decoys.", options)})
337	        return int(answers["c"]["choice"])
338	
339	    async def repair(self, obs: Observation, position: str | None):
340	        """The page does not advance: Qwen reads it (validation messages) and chooses corrective actions."""
341	        system = ("You enter a finished tender bid into a web form. The values are final: never change them, only "
342	                  "enter them as the form expects. Reply with JSON {\"actions\": [...]} using the ops click, fill, "
343	                  "select and check with control ids of the page, e.g. {\"op\": \"fill\", \"id\": 7, \"value\": \"1.234,50\"}.")
344	        user = (f"SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS:\n{self.brief_submission}\n\nVALUES FOR THIS PAGE: "
345	                f"{json.dumps(self.values_for(position), ensure_ascii=False)}\nPOSITIONS IN THE BID: {list(self.positions)}"
346	                f" (omit any other position)\n\nPAGE (it did not advance; read its messages):\n{obs.clip(20000)}")
347	        try:
348	            reply = await llm.qwen(system, user, max_tokens=800)
349	        except Exception as error:
350	            self.log(f"[submit] repair failed: {error}")
351	            return
352	        for action in (reply.get("actions") or [])[:10]:
353	            try:
354	                cid, op = int(action["id"]), action.get("op")
355	                if op == "click":
356	                    result = await self.tab.click(cid)
357	                elif op == "select":
358	                    result = await self.tab.select(cid, action.get("option") or action.get("value", ""))
359	                elif op == "check":
360	                    result = await self.tab.check(cid, bool(action.get("on", True)))
361	                else:
362	                    result = await self.tab.fill(cid, action.get("value", ""))
363	                self.log(f"[submit] repair: {result}")
364	            except Exception as error:
365	                self.log(f"[submit] repair action failed: {error}")
366	                break
367	
368	    async def fetch_tan(self, obs: Observation, until: float) -> str | None:
369	        """The mail worker opens the newest TAN message for this tender and reports the code as a note."""
370	        if not self.mail:
371	            return None
372	        request = re.findall(r"(?:Anforderung|request)\D{0,5}(\d+)", obs.text, re.I)
373	        goal = (f"Read the newest signing TAN message for {self.answer['tender_reference']}"
374	                + (f" (request {request[-1]})" if request else "")
375	                + " (new TAN messages appear at the top of the inbox without a search; open its message URL with "
376	                  "read) and return the code in the reply field 'tan'. Older TAN messages are invalid.")
377	        self.mail.result.pop("tan", None)
378	        self.mail.assign([goal], fresh=True)
379	        worker = asyncio.create_task(self.mail.run(min(until, llm.clock() + 90), max_steps=self.mail.steps + 25))
380	        try:
381	            while not worker.done() and not self.mail.result.get("tan"):
382	                await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
383	            return self.mail.result.get("tan")
384	        finally:
385	            worker.cancel()

1	"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.
2	
3	solve() runs three phases, each as short as the evidence allows:
4	1. The master (Qwen, no website access) turns the brief into goals per website, while the workers' browsers
5	   already sign in and clear the start-up obstacles.
6	2. One worker per website (its own browser, at most 4) gathers typed evidence: Clef (clef-flash) is the click
7	   policy, Qwen reads pages, types searches and solves gates. Workers share facts on a board, so one website's facts
8	   steer another's searches. Research ends as soon as every worker is done, or earlier once the calculator finds no
9	   gap and the tender and mail workers are done; a hard deadline and per-worker step, turn and wait budgets bound it.
10	3. The master decides the bid from the evidence (the brief's formulas computed exactly by pricing.py, a Qwen review
11	   and one round of follow-ups only when gaps remain), enters it in the submission website and signs it with the TAN
12	   the mail worker fetches. The submission form is opened and its bidder page filled in a tab of its own as soon as
13	   the submission website's worker is done, so only the bid's values remain once the bid is decided.
14	Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
15	"""

51	async def open_tabs(task: dict, page) -> dict[str, Tab]:
52	    """One browser per website (the run's browsers over CDP; locally, Chromiums of our own), attached in parallel."""
53	    count = max(1, len(browsers.cdp_urls())) if browsers.cdp_urls() else len(task["access"])
54	
55	    async def attach(index: int, site: dict) -> Tab:
56	        if index == 0:
57	            context, site_page = page.context, page
58	        elif index < count and PLAYWRIGHT is not None:
59	            _, site_page = await browsers.connect(PLAYWRIGHT, min(index, 3))
60	            context = site_page.context
61	        else:  # more websites than browsers: a separate context in browser 1
62	            context = await page.context.browser.new_context()
63	            site_page = await context.new_page()
64	        await site_page.set_viewport_size({"width": 1280, "height": 800})
65	        return Tab(site, context, site_page, log)
66	
67	    tabs = await asyncio.gather(*(attach(index, site) for index, site in enumerate(task["access"])))
68	    return {site["siteId"]: tab for site, tab in zip(task["access"], tabs)}

71	def bid_from(board: Board, plan: dict, brief: str) -> dict:
72	    reference = plan.get("reference") or ""
73	    scenario = plan.get("scenario_date") or ""
74	    if not reference:
75	        found = re.search(r"\(([A-Z]{1,6}-\d{4}-\d{2,6})\)", brief)
76	        reference = found.group(1) if found else ""
77	    try:
78	        return pricing.calculate_bid(board.evidence, reference, scenario)
79	    except Exception as error:  # malformed evidence must not stop the signed submission
80	        log(f"[master] calculator error: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
81	        return {"answer": {"tender_reference": reference, "decision": "bid", "currency": "EUR",
82	                           "discount_percent": 0.0, "positions": [], "total_net": 0.0},
83	                "gaps": [f"calculator error: {error}"], "details": [], "omitted": []}

88	    positions = bid["answer"]["positions"]

90	        all(key in entry for key in ("lead_time_weeks", "base_unit_price", "surcharge_per_unit", "packaging_per_unit",

100	def bidder_emails(review: dict, plan: dict, board: Board, mail_site: str | None) -> list[str]:
101	    """The bidder's own address: the review's or plan's reading first, then addresses the mailbox worker noted."""
102	    found = [value for value in (review.get("bidder_email"), (plan.get("bidder") or {}).get("email"))
103	             if isinstance(value, str) and "@" in value]
104	    notes = [note for note in board.notes if note.startswith(f"[{mail_site}]")] or board.notes
105	    found += re.findall(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(?:\.[\w-]+)+", "\n".join(notes))
106	    return list(dict.fromkeys(found))

109	async def solve(task: dict, page) -> dict | None:
110	    start = llm.clock()
111	    trace_dir = Path(os.environ.get("AGENT_TRACE_DIR", ".runs"))
112	    trace_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
113	    agents.TRACE = trace_dir / f"trace-{int(time.time())}.jsonl"
114	    end = start + min(contract.seconds_left(task) - 50, 19.2 * 60)
115	    research_end = min(start + 7 * 60, end - 6.5 * 60)  # a hard cap: research normally ends when its workers are done
116	    brief = brief_without_credentials(task["brief"])
117	    sites = [{"siteId": site["siteId"], "url": site["url"]} for site in task["access"]]
118	    system = COMMON.format(brief=brief, sites=json.dumps(sites))
119	    board = Board()
120	    tabs = await open_tabs(task, page)
121	    workers = {site["siteId"]: Worker(site, tabs[site["siteId"]], board, system, log) for site in task["access"]}
122	    master = Master(system, sites, log)
123	
124	    # Phase 1: the master plans while the workers sign in (obstacles need no plan).
125	    running = [asyncio.create_task(worker.run(research_end)) for worker in workers.values()]
126	    helpers: list[Worker] = []
127	
128	    async def spawn(parent: Worker, goal: str) -> str:
129	        """A worker delegates an independent part of its goals to a helper in a new tab of its session."""
130	        mine = [helper for helper in helpers if helper.id == parent.id]
131	        if len(mine) >= 2 or len(goal) < 15 or research_end - llm.clock() < 60:
132	            return "no helper available: do it yourself"
133	        tab = Tab(parent.site, parent.tab.context, await parent.tab.context.new_page(), log)
134	        helper = Worker(parent.site, tab, board, system, log, name=f"{parent.id}#{len(mine) + 1}")
135	        helper.assign([goal])
136	        helper.history.append(f"started by the {parent.id} worker, which continues with the other parts")
137	        helpers.append(helper)
138	        await tab.goto(parent.tab.page.url)
139	        running.append(asyncio.create_task(helper.run(research_end, max_steps=30)))
140	        return f"helper {helper.name} started: {goal[:120]}"
141	
142	    for worker in workers.values():
143	        worker.spawn = spawn
144	    plan = await master.make_plan()
145	    for site_id, worker in workers.items():
146	        worker.assign(plan["goals"].get(site_id, []) + [f"share early: {item}" for item in plan["share"].get(site_id, [])][:2])
147	    log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] plan ready")
148	
149	    portal = submission_site(task) if task["submission"].get("kind") == "site" else None
150	    mail_site = mailbox(plan, workers)
151	    submitter, submitting = None, None
152	
153	    def start_submission():
154	        """Open the submission form in a tab of its own and fill what does not depend on the bid."""
155	        nonlocal submitter, submitting
156	        if submitting or portal not in tabs:
157	            return
158	        submitter = Submitter(Tab(tabs[portal].site, tabs[portal].context, None, log), workers.get(mail_site),
159	                              plan, brief, log)
160	        submitting = asyncio.create_task(submitter.run(end, start_url=tabs[portal].page.url))
161	        log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] submission form opened while research continues")
162	
163	    # Phase 2: the workers gather evidence until they are done, the evidence is complete, or the hard deadline.
164	    jobs = dict(zip(workers, running))
165	    first = {job: site for site, job in jobs.items()}
166	    complete_since = None
167	    while llm.clock() < research_end:
168	        active = [job for job in running if not job.done()]
169	        if not active:
170	            break
171	        if portal in jobs and not submitting and jobs[portal].done():
172	            start_submission()
173	        draft = bid_from(board, plan, brief)
174	        essential = [jobs[site] for site in (portal, mail_site) if site in jobs]
175	        if complete(draft) and all(job.done() for job in essential):
176	            complete_since = complete_since or llm.clock()
177	            if llm.clock() - complete_since >= 8:  # a short grace for records still on their way
178	                log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] evidence complete; stopping the remaining workers")
179	                break
180	        else:
181	            complete_since = None
182	        changed = asyncio.ensure_future(board.changed.wait())
183	        await asyncio.wait(active + [changed], timeout=min(10, max(1, research_end - llm.clock())),
184	                           return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
185	        changed.cancel()
186	        for job in active:
187	            if job.done() and job in first:
188	                log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] {first[job]} worker finished")
189	    for job in running:
190	        job.cancel()
191	    await asyncio.wait(running, timeout=5)  # let cancelled workers unwind before anyone reuses their tabs
192	    log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] research finished; {len(board.evidence.records)} records; {llm.USAGE}")
193	
194	    # Phase 3: decide the bid; a review and one round of follow-ups only while gaps remain and time allows.
195	    bid = bid_from(board, plan, brief)
196	    review = {}
197	    if bid["gaps"] or not bid["answer"]["positions"]:
198	        review = await master.review(board, bid)
199	        board.add("master", review.get("records") or [], [])
200	        bid = bid_from(board, plan, brief)
201	        followups = {site: goal for site, goal in (review.get("followups") or {}).items() if site in workers and goal}
202	        if followups and bid["gaps"] and end - llm.clock() > 7 * 60:
203	            log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] follow-ups: {followups}")
204	            until = min(llm.clock() + 120, end - 6 * 60)
205	            for site, goal in followups.items():
206	                workers[site].assign([str(goal)])
207	            await asyncio.gather(*(workers[site].run(until, max_steps=workers[site].steps + 15) for site in followups))
208	            bid = bid_from(board, plan, brief)
209	    log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] bid: " + json.dumps(bid["answer"], ensure_ascii=False))
210	    log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] gaps: " + ("; ".join(bid["gaps"]) or "none") + f" | {review.get('comment', '')}")
211	
212	    if task["submission"].get("kind") == "api":
213	        return bid["answer"]
214	    if portal is None:
215	        log("[master] the submission website is not among the run's websites; nothing submitted")
216	        return None
217	    start_submission()
218	    submitter.set_bid(bid, bidder_emails(review, plan, board, mail_site))
219	    receipt = await submitting
220	    log(f"{llm.stamp()} [master] {'submitted' if receipt else 'NOT submitted'}; {llm.USAGE}")
221	    return None

224	async def main() -> int:
225	    global PLAYWRIGHT

**Copy the 98.7 package from run `f54765` (the compact Qwen + Clef line).** I read the source of both packages before answering.

**Why that one:**

- **Both use the same calculator.** Its `pricing.py` has the same functions as the scored line's, minus five helpers. Pricing mistakes such as the lead time are shared, so choosing it gives up nothing on quality logic.
- **Its weaknesses are narrow enough to fine-tune.** One model call decides whether a follow-up round runs, which is the whole 98.7-versus-35.6 gap. The signing-code step loops. The mail worker stops early.
- **The scored line's weakness is structural.** It makes one Qwen call per browser step, 220–460 calls a run, and that is where 52–83% of its money goes. Tuning does not remove that. Its best is 255 $·s; ranks 4–7 on the board sit at 50–82 $·s, and `f54765` is at 50.
- **Its form filler is general.** Clef maps each control to a bid field once per page layout, then code fills it. I found one line with practice-site wording in the whole package. It also finds the position by reading the page, so the shuffled position order that broke `a489b7` does not affect it.
- **It matches what you asked for:** one worker per site, one master, about 2,700 lines.

**What you take on:**

- **It is the least proven.** It has two runs on this package and four on the line, with no tests. The scored line has ten runs at 35 or more and five test files.
- **It has never been through review.** The scored line has passed four times.

**Decision for you (fair play):** its click helper opens the address of a link the page has disabled (`web.py` line 378, commented "a locked overlay disables the link, not its target"). In `f54765` it opened a mail that way, without doing the slider and checkbox. The scored line does not do this; it refuses any link the model has not observed. Whether a reviewer accepts it is the same question you parked on our own branch. Do you want it kept, or removed before we build on it?

Whichever you choose, keep the reviewed 100 as the submitted package until the new base scores 100 more than once.

If you say go, I will import the package as a separate local branch next to the others. I will not push it or start any runs.
