async def click(self, cid: int) -> str:
        control, locator = self._locate(cid)
        if control.disabled and control.href:  # a locked overlay disables the link, not its target
            await self.goto(control.href)
            return f"opened the target of {control.describe()[:120]}"
        started = self.started
        try:
            await locator.evaluate(OPEN_DETAILS_JS, timeout=2000)
            # no_wait_after: the click returns once it is dispatched, so a slow answer can never make it look
            # failed and be sent a second time; settle() below waits for the navigation it started
            await locator.click(timeout=1500, no_wait_after=True)
        except Exception:
            try:
                await locator.evaluate("e => e.click()", timeout=2000)
            except Exception:
                if not control.href:
                    raise
                await self.goto(control.href)
                return f"clicked {control.describe()[:120]}"
        await self.settle(started)
        return f"clicked {control.describe()[:120]}"

    async def fill(self, cid: int, value: str) -> str:
        control, locator = self._locate(cid)
        value = str(value)
        if control.kind in ("range", "slider"):
            await locator.evaluate("""(e, v) => { const set = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set;
                set.call(e, v); e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); e.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); }""", value, timeout=3000)
            return f"set {control.label} to {value}"
        if control.kind == "select":
            return await self.select(cid, value)
        await locator.evaluate(OPEN_DETAILS_JS, timeout=3000)
        await locator.fill(value, timeout=4000)
        return f"filled {control.label!r} with {value!r}"

    async def select(self, cid: int, option: str) -> str:
        control, locator = self._locate(cid)
        options = control.options or []
        chosen = match_option(option, options)
        if chosen is None:
            raise ValueError(f"no option matches {option!r}; options are {options[:40]}")

                    raise
                await self.goto(control.href)
                return f"clicked {control.describe()[:120]}"
        await self.settle(started)
        return f"clicked {control.describe()[:120]}"

    async def fill(self, cid: int, value: str) -> str:
        control, locator = self._locate(cid)
        value = str(value)
        if control.kind in ("range", "slider"):
            await locator.evaluate("""(e, v) => { const set = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set;
                set.call(e, v); e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles: true})); e.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); }""", value, timeout=3000)
            return f"set {control.label} to {value}"
        if control.kind == "select":
            return await self.select(cid, value)
        await locator.evaluate(OPEN_DETAILS_JS, timeout=3000)
        await locator.fill(value, timeout=4000)
        # typing behind a dialog reports success and changes nothing: read the field back
        after = await locator.evaluate("e => e.value", timeout=2000)
        if value and after != value and after == (control.value or ""):
            raise Blocked(f"typing into {control.label!r} had no effect: something covers it or the page changed")
        return f"filled {control.label!r} with {value!r}"

    async def select(self, cid: int, option: str) -> str:
        control, locator = self._locate(cid)
        options = control.options or []
        chosen = match_option(option, options)
        if chosen is None:
            raise ValueError(f"no option matches {option!r}; options are {options[:40]}")
        started = self.started
        await locator.select_option(label=chosen, timeout=4000, no_wait_after=True)
        after = await locator.evaluate("e => e.selectedIndex >= 0 ? e.options[e.selectedIndex].text : ''", timeout=2000)
        if normalize(after) != normalize(chosen):
            raise Blocked(f"choosing {chosen!r} in {control.label!r} had no effect: something covers it or the page changed")
        await self.settle(started)
        return f"selected {chosen!r} in {control.label!r}"

    async def check(self, cid: int, on: bool = True, strict: bool = False) -> str:
        control, locator = self._locate(cid)
        cover = await self._cover(locator)
        if cover and strict:
            raise Blocked(f"'{cover}' covers {control.describe()[:80]}")
        try:
            if cover:
                raise Blocked(cover)
            await locator.set_checked(on, timeout=3000)
        except Exception:
            if bool(control.checked) != on:
                await locator.evaluate("e => e.click()", timeout=3000)
        return f"{'checked' if on else 'unchecked'} {control.label!r}"

    def overlay(self, obs: Observation) -> list[int]:
        """The controls of an open dialog that lies over the form (not a dialog that holds form fields itself)."""
        found = re.search(r"\[dialog[^\]]*\](.*?)\[/dialog\]", obs.text, re.S)
        ids = [int(number) for number in re.findall(r"\[(\d+):", found.group(1))] if found else []
        ids = [cid for cid in ids if cid in obs.controls]
        holds_fields = any(self.fields.get((obs.controls[cid].kind, obs.controls[cid].label), "other") != "other" for cid in ids)
        return [] if holds_fields else ids

    async def step(self, obs: Observation, kind: str, position: str | None, repeats: int, until: float) -> bool:

        the run without a receipt."""
        tab = self.tab
        covering = self.overlay(obs)
        if covering:  # a dialog over the form goes first: nothing behind it can be typed or clicked
            close = next((cid for cid in covering
                          if self.purposes.get((obs.controls[cid].kind, obs.controls[cid].label)) == "close"), None)
            if close is None:
                close = await self.choose(obs, "close the dialog that covers the form, without following its links", covering)
            self.log(f"[submit] overlay: {await tab.click(close)}")

            await self.repair(obs, position)

            target = close.id if close and kind == "obstacle" else await self.choose(

async def fetch_tan(self, until: float) -> str | None:
        """The mail worker reads the signing TAN that was just requested and reports the code.

        The mailbox's entry page is read in a tab of its own until it shows something it did not show before the
        request (the new message); the model then opens that message and returns the code. Nothing has to be
        searched or unlocked on the way, and the state of the mail worker's main tab does not matter."""
        if not self.mail:
            return None
        pages, patience = [], llm.clock() + 8
        while True:
            try:
                pages = list(await self.mail.tab.read_pages([self.mail.site["url"]]))
            except Exception as error:
                self.log(f"[submit] mailbox not readable: {type(error).__name__}")
            new = set(re.findall(r"→(\S+)", pages[0][1])) - self.mailbox_before if pages else set()
            if new or llm.clock() > patience:
                break
            await asyncio.sleep(0.4)
        goal = (f"A signing TAN for {self.answer['tender_reference']} was requested a moment ago (request number "
                f"{self.tan_requests} of this run) and arrives as a new message. You are given the mailbox as it is "
                "now" + (f"; these links are new since the request: {' '.join(sorted(new))[:300]}" if new else "")
                + ". Open that newest TAN message as its own page with read and return its code in the reply field "
                "'tan'. TAN messages of earlier requests are invalid. If the new message is not listed yet, read "
                "the mailbox address again.")
        self.mail.result.pop("tan", None)
        self.mail.assign([goal], fresh=True)
        self.mail.pending = pages
        worker = asyncio.create_task(self.mail.run(min(until, llm.clock() + 60), max_steps=self.mail.steps + 10))
        try:
            while not worker.done() and not self.mail.result.get("tan"):
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
            return self.mail.result.get("tan")

"""One block per test run started with test_run.py: python live_view.py <label> [<label> ...] [--detail]

Shows the score, cost and time, where the run's seconds went (the agent's own clock), what lost points, and the
log lines that say something went wrong or waited.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
LIVE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "live"
detail = "--detail" in sys.argv
for label in [word for word in sys.argv[1:] if not word.startswith("--")]:
    folder = LIVE / label
    summary = (folder / "get_run.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8") if (folder / "get_run.txt").exists() else ""
    log = (folder / "log.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if (folder / "log.txt").exists() else []
    lines = [re.sub(r"^\[[\d:.]+\] stdout: ?", "", line) for line in log]
    score = re.search(r"^Score: (.*)$", summary, re.M)
    status = re.search(r"^Status (.*)$", summary, re.M)
    print("=" * 110)
    print(f"{label}: " + (score.group(1) if score else (status.group(1) if status else "still running") + f" ({len(lines)} log lines)"))

    def at(pattern):
        for line in lines:
            if re.search(pattern, line):
                found = re.match(r"\s*([\d.]+)s", line)
                return float(found.group(1)) if found else None
        return None

    marks = [("plan", r"\[master\] plan ready"), ("research end", r"research finished"), ("bid", r"\[master\] bid:"),
             ("form start", r"bid received"), ("code asked", r"TAN|request_tan|code request"), ("code typed", r"filled 'Signatur|filled .*TAN"),
             ("signed", r"submit: clicked")]
    times = [(name, at(pattern)) for name, pattern in marks]
    print("  clock: " + " | ".join(f"{name} {value:.0f}s" for name, value in times if value is not None))
    workers = [line for line in lines if "stopped after" in line]
    print("  workers: " + " ; ".join(re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)[:90] for line in workers[:8]))
    if summary:
        lost = re.findall(r"^\s+([\w\[\]\.]+): 0 \(entered (.*?)\)$", summary, re.M)
        lost = [(name, value) for name, value in lost if name != "extra_positions"]
        zero = re.findall(r"^\s+(index_window|withdrawn_answer): 0", summary, re.M)
        print("  lost: " + ("; ".join(f"{name}={value}" for name, value in lost[:14]) + (" " + " ".join(zero) if zero else "") or "nothing"))
    patterns = r"waited [\d.]+s|rejected:|reading the page again|overlay|not accepted|timed out|failed|giving up|server error|gaps:|open gaps|evidence complete|keeps returning"
    notable = [line for line in lines if re.search(patterns, line)]
    for line in (notable if detail else notable[:14]):
        print("    " + re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)[:200])
    if not detail and len(notable) > 14:
        print(f"    ... {len(notable) - 14} more such lines")

No candidate beat the submitted a2, so keep a2 as the team's entry; nothing new was submitted.

Final test runs in this window (the platform and practice sites were slow throughout):

| Run | Commit | Quality | Eligible | Cost | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a3 | `7bb935d` (the submitted a2 package, rerun) | 0 | no | $0.0989 | 07:47 |
| d1 | `b26cfc6` | 10 | yes | $0.1057 | 06:31 |
| e1 | `1aa0080` | 10 | yes | $0.1133 | 07:25 |
| e2 | `1aa0080` | 42.1 | yes | $0.1373 | 03:03 |
| f1 | `aa65827` | 75.7 | yes | $0.2081 | 04:05 |
| f2 | `aa65827` | 43.4 | yes | $0.1608 | 05:22 |
| g1 | `663c449` | 35.6 | yes | $0.0883 | 03:43 |

- **The candidates:** every run since the mail-search fix (`b26cfc6`) got a bid submitted and was eligible, but none reached 100, and they cost 1.3 to 3 times as much as a2's $0.068. The best was 75.7.
- **The submitted package:** its rerun scored 0 under today's load. Research ran long, the bid had gaps, and the form filler looped on a delivery-time field until the deadline. Its record is now one 100, one partial bid and one 0.
- **Why I'd still keep a2:** the final is best of 3, and a2 is the only package that has scored 100. The candidates trade that ceiling for always being eligible at 35–76.

Fixes made and committed locally on `claude-fast` in this window:
- **Form filler retries** (`1aa0080`): it takes the form up again after a failed page load or model call instead of ending with no answer. This rescued e2, which would otherwise have scored 0.
- **Entry address always known** (`aa65827`): my rule against made-up addresses was refusing a website's own start address after a slow first load, which cost d1 and e1 a whole website. A page that did not load is now reopened without a model turn, and page loads get 30 s instead of 15 s.
- **No clicks off the run's website** (`663c449`): in e2 the form filler followed a footer link to another site from the signing page.
- **Blocked typing names the dialog** (`1aa0080`): the worker now closes it within a few seconds instead of retrying blind.

What still loses points is evidence gathering, not the form:
- The mail worker stops before all calculation mails are read (FX rate, project bonus, setup pool, end reserves).
- The metal index was not found in f1; that alone cost its 24 points.
- The ERP worker waits on mail.

One loose end: the commit of `CLAUDE.md` in the main repository is still hanging in Entire's commit hook. The file is staged and nothing is lost; I have not skipped the hook. Tell me if you want it committed with the hook skipped.

export const meta = {

  description: 'Find, per website worker, why candidate runs miss evidence that the 100-point run found, and propose general mechanisms',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Diagnose', detail: 'one analyst per worker and one for orchestration, across six run logs' },
    { title: 'Challenge', detail: 'a skeptic checks each proposed mechanism against the logs and the rules' },
  ],
}

const LIVE = 'C:\\Users\\ADMINI~1\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\claude\\c--Users-Administrator-Documents-GitHub-The-Last-Team\\c8b91696-6cf4-42bb-80ed-10d1928a6515\\scratchpad\\live'
const CODE = 'C:\\Users\\Administrator\\Documents\\GitHub\\The-Last-Team-fast'

const COMMON = `
You are diagnosing an autonomous bidding agent (hackathon challenge "From RFQ to bid"). It sends one worker per
website (tender-portal, customer-portal, erp, mail), each in its own browser; workers publish records to a shared
board; a calculator prices the bid; a form filler submits it. Read-only task: do NOT edit files, do NOT start runs,
do NOT touch git. Return analysis only.

Code (current candidate, HEAD of branch claude-fast): ${CODE}
  agent.py (orchestration, research deadline, gap round), agents.py (prompts COMMON/WORKER/PLAN/REVIEW, Board,
  Worker with a cheap click-policy model "Clef" in decide() and the reasoning model "Qwen" in think(), Master),
  web.py (page rendering, actions, read_pages), submit.py (form filler), pricing.py (RECORD_GUIDE, calculator, gaps).

Run logs (one folder per run, file log.txt; get_run.txt holds the score and points per field):
  ${LIVE}\\a2   quality 100 (older commit 7bb935d; this is the REFERENCE: it found every fact)
  ${LIVE}\\f1   quality 75.7 (final gap: metal index for every position)
  ${LIVE}\\f2   quality 43.4 (gaps: FX rate, project bonus, base prices for the discount threshold)
  ${LIVE}\\g1   quality 35.6 (mail worker gave up early; many gaps)
  ${LIVE}\\e2   quality 42.1 (gaps: end reserves, matching materials, setup pool, project bonus, delivery commitment)
  ${LIVE}\\a3   quality 0 (same package as a2, rerun under load)
Log line format: "[mm:ss.s] stdout:  <seconds>s [<worker>] <kind>: <text>". "+ <kind>: ..." is an accepted record.
"rejected:" is a record refused by validation. "[master] gaps: ..." lists what the calculator still lacks.
"gather:"/"obstacle:"/"act:" lines are actions chosen by the click-policy model; "read:/act:/stuck: +N records; next: ..."
lines are reasoning-model turns. Lines are cut at about 300 characters. Use Grep with line numbers; logs are 400-800 lines.

Hard rules for any fix you propose:
- General mechanisms only. No special cases, no site-specific values: never put labels, hostnames, paths, document
  names, identifiers or anything else seen on these practice websites into code or prompts. The final ranking is on a
  private dataset with other layouts and wording.
- Fair play: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at
  runtime. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set,
  calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. Helpers must not crawl a website on their own to assemble the evidence.
- Keep it light: prefer ONE small mechanism that removes a whole class of failure over several guards. A fix that
  adds model turns or cost must say so. Ranking: eligible, then quality, then LLM cost x run time.
- Evidence first: every claim cites run label and log line number(s). If you cannot tell from the logs, say so.

          change: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete change: file, function, what to add/remove, including any prompt wording (free of website values)' },
          points_at_stake: { type: 'string' },
          cost_effect: { type: 'string', description: 'effect on model turns, time and cost' },

const SCOPES = [

**Written for:** Claude Design, building a pitch-deck slide for a non-technical audience. This describes the agent that is on the leaderboard.

```
HOW IT WORKS: FROM REQUEST TO SIGNED BID IN ABOUT THREE MINUTES

The job
A customer sends a request for a quote. Answering it means logging in to four
different business websites (the tender portal, the customer's document portal,
the company's ERP system and a mailbox), finding the right facts in each, working
out a price, filling in the bid form and signing it. A person needs hours.
Our agent does it alone.

The pipeline, step by step

1. Read the request
   The agent reads the request and the list of websites it may use.

2. Make a plan
   A planning model writes a short list of goals for each website:
   what to look for there and why.

3. Four workers, four websites, at the same time
   Each website gets its own worker with its own browser. A worker behaves like
   a careful employee: it logs in, closes pop-ups, passes the gates, searches,
   opens documents and writes down the facts it finds.
   - A small, fast model picks the next click.
   - A stronger model reads the pages and decides what matters.

4. One shared board
   Every fact goes onto a shared board that all workers can see. A fact found on
   one website steers the search on another. Example: the product group in the
   customer's specification tells the ERP worker what to search for.
   Every number on the board must appear on a page the worker really saw.
   Nothing is invented.

5. Check what is missing
   The calculator lists the facts it still lacks. The workers get one more
   focused round to find exactly those.

6. Calculate the bid
   Plain code does all the arithmetic, exact to the cent: the right product,
   the right price for the quantity, surcharges, packaging, discounts, delivery
   time, the total. No AI model does maths.

7. Fill in the form
   A model looks at the bid form once and says which field means what.
   Code then types the values and reads each one back to make sure it arrived.
   A position that cannot be priced safely is left out, never guessed.

8. Sign and submit
   The agent asks for a signing code, picks it up from the mailbox, signs the
   bid and submits it.

The three ideas behind it
- AI decides, code executes. Models choose where to go and what to read.
  Code does the maths and the typing, where mistakes are not allowed.
- Never guess. A missing fact stays missing. A wrong price is worse than no price.
- No waiting around. The agent moves on the moment a page has answered,
  instead of pausing for a fixed time. That alone cut a run from over six
  minutes to about three.

Numbers to quote (our scored run)
Quality 100 out of 100. Cost: about 7 cents. Time: 3 minutes 18 seconds.
Two small hosted models, no frontier model.

Suggested visual
A left-to-right flow: Request -> Plan -> four parallel lanes (Tender portal,
Customer portal, ERP, Mailbox) -> Shared board -> Calculator -> Bid form ->
Signature -> Submitted. Mark the four lanes as "AI decides" and the calculator
and form as "code executes".
```

"""One-off patch: gap lines name the requirement and catalog group; one material number keeps one set of
attributes; the follow-up goal says that a listed fact is not recorded yet."""
import io
import sys

ROOT = sys.argv[1]
BS = chr(92)
N = BS + "n"


def patch(name, pairs):
    path = ROOT + "/" + name
    s = io.open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="").read()
    nl = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in s else "\n"
    for old, new in pairs:
        old, new = old.replace("\n", nl), new.replace("\n", nl)
        assert s.count(old) == 1, (name, s.count(old), old[:80])
        s = s.replace(old, new)
    io.open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write(s)


patch("pricing.py", [
    # gap lines say which requirement and catalog group a position stands for
    ('''        spec, problem = required_for(position.get("requirement_ref"))
        if problem:
            line["gaps"].append(problem)
''',
     '''        spec, problem = required_for(position.get("requirement_ref"))
        if problem:
            line["gaps"].append(problem)
        line["_about"] = ", ".join(part for part in (
            f"requirement {position['requirement_ref']}" if position.get("requirement_ref") else "",
            f"catalog group {spec['catalog_group']}" if spec and spec.get("catalog_group") else "") if part)
'''),
    ('''        gaps.extend(f"{line['position']}: {gap}" for gap in line["gaps"])
''',
     '''        about = f" ({line['_about']})" if line.get("_about") else ""
        gaps.extend(f"{line['position']}{about}: {gap}" for gap in line["gaps"])
'''),
    # one material number, one set of attributes
    ('''        problems = validate(kind, data)
        if not problems:
            self.records.append({"kind": kind, "data": data, "source": source})
        return problems
''',
     '''        problems = validate(kind, data)
        if not problems and kind == "material":
            problems = self.contradicts(data)
        if not problems:
            self.records.append({"kind": kind, "data": data, "source": source})
        return problems

    def contradicts(self, data: dict) -> list[str]:
        """A material number stands for one article: a record that gives a recorded number another catalog group
        or other technical attributes has mixed two articles up."""
        number_ = norm_ref(data.get("material_number"))
        problems = []
        for earlier in self.of("material"):
            if norm_ref(earlier.get("material_number")) != number_:
                continue
            for attribute in ("catalog_group",) + ATTRIBUTES:
                old, new = earlier.get(attribute), data.get(attribute)
                if old in (None, "") or new in (None, ""):
                    continue
                same = norm_ref(old) == norm_ref(new) if attribute == "catalog_group" else same_attribute(attribute, old, new)
                if not same:
                    problems.append(f"material {data.get('material_number')} was recorded with {attribute}={old}; "
                                    f"{attribute}={new} belongs to another material number: check the number on the page")
            if problems:
                break
        return problems[:2]
'''),
])
